name: Cynthia Barrett
life: “I still remember the first word I wrote under a lunch tin.” On Monday, near the corner by Juniper Tailor, Cynthia looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I wrote an alphabet on the inside of my lunch tin so I could practice without answering questions.
appearance: Cynthia has brown hair pinned away from the temples, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a little coil of soft measuring tape. When somebody else has the floor, Cynthia looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Cynthia never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Cynthia can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To read a whole page without hiding the practice.
family: Ivan Ruiz is Cynthia’s second cousin. Cynthia offers the first invitation. Ivan gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The gift nobody wants*, Ivan says, “I would give my right arm to inherit a place.”
connections: Morgan Gil. An adult practicing after a flour shift shares a quiet place with the learner practicing on a tin.

reactions.situation: A pupil chooses another language halfway through the reading
reactions.response: Cynthia lets the pupil finish in the language they chose.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Cynthia offers to help correct the printed name and leaves it to the colleague whether any public explanation is wanted.

reactions.situation: When a relative hints at needing company
reactions.response: Cynthia may initially offer a repair, but sits down as soon as the request becomes clear.
